alerts.reason: Astec's June net sales rose just 4.8% while its order backlog grew 139.7% year over year to $436.1 million (A, C). The order book supports a September quarter above −5%. My forecast of a December crossing rests on the reported labor shortages persisting long enough to push equipment shipments beyond year-end (D).

Citrix's June total net revenue grew only 1.6% despite 73.9% growth in subscription annual recurring revenue (A, B). Since December, deferred maintenance and support revenue had fallen $178.1 million, exceeding the $168.9 million increase in deferred subscription revenue (C). I expect subscription growth to keep September above −5%, with the shrinking maintenance balance contributing less revenue by December and taking the year-over-year change to −5% or lower.

Take-Two's June net bookings fell $284.8 million year over year across several franchises, while recognized net revenue fell only $18.0 million (B, E). Grand Theft Auto alone supplied 33.7% of quarterly net revenue and contributed to the bookings decline (A, B). I expect earlier bookings to cushion September revenue above −5%, with weaker bookings feeding through to a decline of at least 5% in December.

First Solar's June net sales fell 2%. Higher module volume and a project indemnification settlement partly offset lower project sales and construction activity (A, B). I expect module volume to keep September above −5%. With project sales uneven, the settlement benefit unlikely to recur, and module selling prices under pressure (D), I forecast a December decline of at least 5%.
